Do You Really Need a Full Home Appraisal? When a Desktop Appraisal Makes Sense

Not every property valuation requires an appraiser to walk through the front door.

By Reddy Appraisal LLCOctober 22, 20262 min read

IN THIS ARTICLE

When an interior visit may not be neededA desktop appraisal still requires credible analysisChoose a scope that fits the intended useMore in Appraisal Guides ↗← All 24 articles

THE SHORT ANSWER

For estate planning, private decision-making, and some other non-lending needs in Tucson and Southern Arizona, ask whether a desktop scope of work may be appropriate. Reddy Appraisal LLC can discuss the intended use and available information before determining the suitable appraisal approach.

When an interior visit may not be needed

Not every property valuation requires an appraiser to walk through the front door. For certain private purposes, a desktop appraisal can be a practical way to obtain an independent value opinion using available property records, market data, photographs, and other reliable sources. The right approach depends on the property and how the appraisal will be used.

A desktop appraisal still requires credible analysis

A desktop appraisal is still an appraisal—not simply a computer-generated estimate. The appraiser must have sufficient information to develop a credible result and clearly disclose the scope of work and any important limitations. Unusual properties, major renovations, disputed condition, or certain lender and legal requirements may call for an inspection or a different assignment instead.

Choose a scope that fits the intended use

For estate planning, private decision-making, and some other non-lending needs in Tucson and Southern Arizona, ask whether a desktop scope of work may be appropriate. Reddy Appraisal LLC can discuss the intended use and available information before determining the suitable appraisal approach. A faster or less intrusive process should never come at the expense of a reliable valuation.

About this article

General educational information. The suitable appraisal scope depends on the property, intended use, effective date and available information.
